audit.whatIsWrong: Three of Hwei's abilities are called by invented names across the page: "Subject: Fear (CC Paints)" (used in focus.text, winCon, enemyWin, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[2].d and three report entries), "Severance" (whys[2], spikes[0], early, wants.you[2]) and "Fragment of Dread" (mid).
audit.why: His real abilities are Subject: Disaster (Q, subspells Devastating Fire, Severing Bolt, Molten Fissure), Subject: Serenity (W), Subject: Torment (E, subspells Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw) and Spiraling Despair (R). The packet also flags that the page never names a single one correctly. Beyond the names, the decisive mechanic is absent: Signature of the Visionary primes on the first damaging spell and detonates on the SECOND, so eating one paint and stepping out costs almost nothing while trading through two is the whole burst.
audit.corrected: Every fabricated name replaced with the real one, and the two-spell signature rule is now stated in breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, the trade lines, dontsFull[0].d and the early paragraph.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..3].side read "Skill" while content win[0..3] and the packet levelChart read "Hwei".
audit.why: Hwei out-ranges and out-pokes an immobile Anivia through level 5; Anivia's 46.75% over 1767 games is the worst in this slice and both other sources put the early rows on Hwei.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side = Hwei, matching win[0..3] and the packet chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike named a non-existent ultimate and gave it no numbers.
audit.why: Spiraling Despair is 120/100/80s, reaches 1300, and expands around the first champion it strikes — the range is what makes it a positioning spike rather than an all-in spike.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid and dontsFull[2].d now name it with its range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and every 'wait for X' line pointed at an ability that does not exist.
audit.why: Subject: Torment is 12s at rank 1 and carries all his crowd control; Subject: Disaster costs 80 mana at rank 1, which is what makes forcing him to clear expensive.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, loading, winCon and ahead now key advice to those numbers.

edits.before: Hwei's layered spell-combos give him some of the best poke in the mid lane, and his range plus varied angles let him punish your slow, obvious Q setup at levels 1-2 without much risk. He can weave Devastating Fire and Severance together for chip damage you simply can't answer yet. Play from max range, don't contest waves aggressively, and treat any extended poke war as a loss until you have real answers online — your egg buys time but doesn't erase the damage gap.
edits.after: Hwei's layered spell-combos give him some of the best poke in the mid lane, and his range plus varied angles let him punish your slow, obvious Q at levels 1-2 without much risk. Every second damaging spell on you completes his signature and detonates it, so eat one paint and step out rather than trading through both. Play from max range, don't contest waves, and treat an extended poke war as a loss until your answers are online.

edits.before: Hwei continues to win the poke war through levels 4-5, since his combo damage output and range advantage still exceed anything you can punish with. His ultimate at 6, Fragment of Dread, threatens real burst if he catches you isolated, so respect his all-in potential even as your own Glacial Storm comes online. Once you hit 6, you finally get sustained zone pressure that starts closing the gap, but he still holds a slight edge until your first item lands.
